name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican Tom Sell has massive financial advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~1%
Open seat but no evidence of Democratic competitiveness
model.rationale: TX-19 is a heavily Republican open seat, and the Democratic candidate has raised only about $31K against Sell's $2.1M plus $1.3M in outside support. Markets price a Republican win near 98%, and no polls or ratings suggest competitiveness.
model.watch: A surprise polling error or major scandal involving Sell could narrow the race, but nothing in the evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
West Texas's 19th District is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+25. Jodey Arrington's retirement opens the seat, but the fundamentals still overwhelmingly favor the GOP. Republican Tom Sell has raised over $2.1 million and benefits from more than $1.3 million in outside spending, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $31,000 with minimal cash on hand.

Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 1% chance, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no public polling and no signs of Democratic investment, the forecast sits near the district's baseline: a Republican win by around 20 points, rated Safe R.
